newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens stronger after jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens stronger after jobs report.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger in heavy trading on Friday at C$1.3689 (US$0.7305). * Dealers said Canadian report that employment grew by 51,500 in June, bringing jobless rate down to 9.1 percent, was responsible for the rise. * Market now awaiting U.S. inflation data. If it is tame, Canadian dollar seen firming below C$1.3680 (US$0.7310).
The Canadian dollar strengthened after Statistics Canada reported that employment grew by 51,500 in June, bringing the country's jobless rate down to 9.1 percent from 9.5 percent.
The report confirmed economic growth remains robust and increases the likelihood that the Bank of Canada will raise short-term interest rates again before the end of the year.
Dealers said the market is now focused on the U.S. producer price index for June due for release this morning. A tame report is seen providing the Canadian currency with room to strengthen further.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 82.98 Japanese yen from 82.26 at Thursday's close. The dollar firmed to 1.2856 German marks from 1.2820 marks on Thursday.
